topics.name: Introduction to DSA and Java Setup

questions.title: Above Average Scores
questions.description:
A teacher counts how many students scored strictly above the class average. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int aboveAverage(int[] scores)

Compute the average as a double, then count the elements strictly greater than it.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated scores.

Output Format:
One line with the count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= scores[i] <= 100

questions.title: Aisle Scan Order
questions.description:
A warehouse robot scans shelf trees level by level, left to right within each level — the classic level-order (breadth-first) traversal. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void levelOrder(TNode root, ArrayList<Integer> out)

It must append the node values level by level into out (the harness prints them space-separated). Use a queue of nodes: dequeue one node at a time, record it, then enqueue its children.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of slots in the level-order description. Line 2: n space-separated integers — the shelf tree in level order, -1 marks a missing child.

Output Format:
One line with the scan order space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1 <= value <= 1000, the tree is non-empty
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 2000, -1 <= value <= 1000, the tree is non-empty

questions.title: Alert Prepended to Feed
questions.description:
A monitoring feed pins each new alert at the FRONT of a doubly linked list so the newest shows first. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static DNode insertFront(DNode head, int value)

It must prepend a node holding value (fix both prev and next) and return the new head. The harness prints the feed forwards space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers — the feed entries in order. Line 3: the new alert code.

Output Format:
One line with the feed forwards space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= code <= 1000

questions.title: Anagram Check
questions.description:
A word game validates that two words are anagrams — same letters with the same counts. Compare by counting characters (sorting is forbidden here). Lowercase letters only, case-sensitive. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static boolean isAnagram(String s, String t)

It must return true when t is an anagram of s. The harness prints 1 for true and 0 for false.

Input Format:
One line with the two words.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= length <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Apply Backspace Characters
questions.description:
A keyboard is stuck: every '#' in the typed stream is a backspace that deletes the last character still on the page. The editor itself is a stack — model it that way.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String applyBackspaces(String s)

Process s left to right. A normal character is pushed onto the stack; '#' pops the last character if any. Return the final text (guaranteed non-empty).

Input Format:
One line: the typed string s.

Output Format:
One line: the final text after applying all backspaces.

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s contains lowercase letters and '#'
the final text is guaranteed non-empty
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= s.length <= 1000, lowercase letters and '#', final text non-empty

questions.title: Array Maximum
questions.description:
Find the largest value in an integer array with a single traversal. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int arrayMax(int[] arr)

It must return the largest element.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Array Minimum
questions.description:
Find the smallest value in an integer array with a single traversal. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int arrayMin(int[] arr)

It must return the smallest element.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Array Sum and Average
questions.description:
Traverse an array and accumulate its total. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int arraySum(int[] arr)

It must return the sum of all elements. The harness prints the sum, then the average (sum divided by n, printed to 2 decimals) for you.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: the sum. Line 2: the average rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: ArrayList Middle Element
questions.description:
Practise the java.util.ArrayList API: size() and get(index). The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int middleElement(ArrayList<Integer> list)

The list always holds an odd number of elements. Return the middle element — the one at index size() / 2.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (odd). Line 2: n space-separated integers, added to the list in order.

Output Format:
One line with the middle element.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 9999 (n is odd), -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Assignment Deadline Crunch
questions.description:
Every assignment takes exactly one time slot and must finish by its deadline. Sort the deadlines ascending and greedily fill slots 1, 2, 3, ... — take a job whenever its deadline is still ahead of the clock. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int maxJobs(int[] deadlines)

It must return the maximum number of assignments that can be completed.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n deadlines.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum number of assignments completed.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= deadlines <= 100

questions.title: Autocorrect Edit Cost
questions.description:
An autocorrect engine ranks suggestions by edit distance — the minimum number of insertions, deletions and replacements that turn one word into another. The Wagner–Fischer tabulation fills a two-dimensional DP table over prefixes. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int editDistance(String a, String b)

It must return the Levenshtein distance between the two words.

Input Format:
Two lines: word a, then word b.

Output Format:
One line with the edit distance.

Constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 50

questions.title: Average of Three Numbers
questions.description:
Return a floating-point average from integer inputs. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static double averageThree(int a, int b, int c)

It must return (a + b + c) / 3.0. The harness prints the result rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with three integer marks A, B and C.

Output Format:
One line with the average rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= A, B, C <= 100

questions.title: BFS Traversal
questions.description:
Breadth-first search explores a graph in rings: the start node, then its neighbours, then their neighbours. Neighbours are processed in the order the adjacency list stores them. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void bfs(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int start, ArrayList<Integer> out)

It must append the BFS visit order (starting with start) into out, using a queue and a visited array so no node is visited twice. The harness prints the order space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected edge. Last line: the start node.

Output Format:
One line with the BFS order space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Backbone Path Length
questions.description:
A campus network hangs its buildings off a binary tree; the backbone is the longest path between any two buildings, measured in edges. A useful fact: for each node, the longest path through it joins the deepest ends of its two subtrees. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int diameter(TNode root)

It must return the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes (0 for an empty tree or a single node).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of slots in the level-order description. Line 2: n space-separated integers — the network tree in level order, -1 marks a missing child.

Output Format:
One line with the backbone length in edges.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Balanced Parentheses
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int isBalanced(String s)

Return 1 if the brackets in s are balanced, 0 otherwise. Bracket types are (), [] and {}. Non-bracket rules do not apply — s contains only bracket characters. Use a stack: push opening brackets, match every closing bracket against the top.

Input Format:
One line: the bracket string s.

Output Format:
One line: 1 if balanced, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s contains only the characters ()[]{}

questions.title: Balanced Parentheses in Order
questions.description:
A syntax generator lists every balanced sequence of n bracket pairs in lexicographic order ('(' sorts before ')'): at each position try '(' while any unused pair remains, then ')' while it closes an open bracket — this backtracking order is already lexicographic. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String balancedSet(int n)

It must return all 2n-character sequences in lexicographic order, separated by newline characters (no trailing newline needed).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
The valid sequences, one per line, in lexicographic order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 7

questions.title: Balloon Burst Arrows
questions.description:
Balloons float along a horizontal axis; balloon i spans [start[i], end[i]]. One arrow shot vertically at position x bursts every balloon with start[i] <= x <= end[i]. Sorting balloons by end and shooting each arrow at the earliest-ending balloon's right edge minimises the arrow count. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minArrows(int[] start, int[] end)

It must return the minimum number of arrows needed to burst every balloon.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start coordinates. Line 3: n end coordinates (end[i] >= start[i]).

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of arrows.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= start <= end <= 10000

questions.title: Best Stock Profit Day
questions.description:
A trader reviews a day's prices and wants the largest single gain from buying at hour i and selling LATER at hour j (j > i). Scanning once while tracking the cheapest price so far yields the best difference in O(n); when prices only fall, no profitable pair exists and the answer is -1. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long maxPriceJump(int[] prices)

It must return the maximum prices[j] - prices[i] over j > i, or -1 when no positive difference exists.

Input Format:
Line 1: N. Line 2: N prices.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum gain, or -1.

Constraints:
2 <= N <= 50, 1 <= price <= 2000000000

questions.title: Binary Numbers via a Queue
questions.description:
A number-formatter gadget generates the binary representations of 1..n with a queue of unfinished strings: every dequeued prefix spawns two longer prefixes.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String[] binaryNumbers(int n)

Generate the binary strings for 1 to n in ascending order using a queue (start from "1"; dequeuing "x" enqueues "x0" and "x1"). Do not use Integer.toBinaryString.

Input Format:
One line: integer n.

Output Format:
One line with the n binary strings, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500

questions.title: Binary Search Index
questions.description:
Search a sorted array by halving the range. The array is sorted in ascending order and has distinct values. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int binarySearch(int[] arr, int target)

It must return the index of target, or -1 when it is absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted distinct integers. Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000 <= value, target <= 1000

questions.title: Binary Search Probe Estimate
questions.description:
A librarian who searches a sorted shelf of n books with binary search needs at most floor(log2 n) + 1 probes in the worst case. Estimate the probes. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int binarySteps(int n)

It must return the worst-case probe count: halve n repeatedly and count the halvings, then add 1 (n = 1 needs exactly 1 probe).

Input Format:
One line with the number of books.

Output Format:
One line with the worst-case probe count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000

questions.title: Bitonic Peak Finder
questions.description:
A hiking log first climbs and then descends: values strictly increase up to the summit, then strictly decrease. Locate the summit index with binary search. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int findPeak(int[] arr)

arr is strictly increasing then strictly decreasing (length >= 3, summit strictly inside). It must return the index of the maximum.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (bitonic).

Output Format:
One line with the summit index.

Constraints:
3 <= n <= 100000, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Bracket Checker for Config Files
questions.description:
A deployment tool validates config snippets: every opening bracket must be closed by the matching type in LIFO order. Letters, digits and operators may appear between brackets and are ignored.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int validConfig(String s)

Return 1 if all brackets (), [] and {} in s are balanced and correctly nested, else 0.

Input Format:
One line: the config string s.

Output Format:
One line: 1 if valid, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s contains letters, digits, operators and the brackets ()[]{}

questions.title: Browser Back Button
questions.description:
A browser keeps visited pages on a history stack. Every new page is pushed; pressing Back pops the current page.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int currentPage(int[] visits, int backs)

Push the page ids in visiting order, then press Back backs times (a Back press on an empty history does nothing). Return the current page id, or -1 if the history is empty.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and backs.
Line 2: n space-separated page ids.

Output Format:
One line: the current page id or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= backs <= n
1 <= visits[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Bubble Sort the Array
questions.description:
Implement the classic bubble sort: repeatedly swap adjacent out-of-order pairs until the array is ascending. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void bubbleSort(int[] arr)

Sort arr in place (ascending). The harness prints the array afterwards.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Bubble Versus Selection Swaps
questions.description:
A lab measures both classics on the same data: report the selection-sort swap count AND the bubble-sort swap count. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long[] swapComparison(int[] arr)

It must return {selectionSwaps, bubbleSwaps} — selection swaps only when the suffix minimum is not already in place; bubble swaps every inverted adjacent pair. Use working copies. The harness prints both numbers.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the selection swaps, then the bubble swaps, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 200, -1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Budget Combo Count
questions.description:
A finance team reviews expense items and asks: in how many distinct ways can a target budget be hit exactly by some subset of the items? Counting subset sums is the counting twin of 0/1 knapsack — one pass per item over a rolling table, each item used at most once. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long countSubsets(int target, int[] values)

It must return the number of subsets of values whose elements sum exactly to target.

Input Format:
Line 1: target T and item count N. Line 2: N item values.

Output Format:
One line with the number of subsets.

Constraints:
1 <= T <= 500, 1 <= N <= 25, 1 <= value <= 500

questions.title: Build System Cycle Check
questions.description:
A build orchestrator resolves module dependencies; a directed cycle among modules would deadlock every build. Detect it with a DFS that colours nodes white (0, unvisited), grey (1, on the current stack) and black (2, finished): a cycle exists exactly when an edge reaches a grey node. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int hasCycle(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return 1 if the directed graph contains a cycle, otherwise 0. You may write additional static helpers.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed dependency u depends on v.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Build the Greeting
questions.description:
Strings in Java are immutable: every concatenation creates a NEW string object. Build a greeting from pieces. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String makeGreeting(String name)

It must return "Hello, " + name + "!".

Input Format:
One line with the name (a single token).

Output Format:
One line with the greeting.

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 50, letters only

questions.title: Campus Road Count
questions.description:
A campus map is an undirected graph; facilities planning needs the number of road segments. Each road appears twice across the adjacency lists — once from each end. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int roadCount(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return the number of undirected roads (the total of all adjacency-list sizes divided by 2).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a road between intersections u and v.

Output Format:
One line with the road count.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Candidate Vote Tally
questions.description:
A club election stores every ballot in a log. The returning officer asks for the number of votes one candidate received.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int tallyVotes(String[] votes, String target)

Count how many entries of votes equal target. Build the full frequency map first — that is the drill.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n (ballots) — then the target name on the same line.
Line 2: n space-separated candidate names.

Output Format:
One line: the vote count for target.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= names.length <= 20, lowercase letters

questions.title: Cargo Value Maximizer
questions.description:
A cargo drone has a weight limit and items can be SLICED: any fraction of an item may be taken, contributing proportional value. The fractional knapsack greedy sorts items by value/weight ratio and fills the drone with whole items, finally slicing the first item that does not fit. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static double fractionalKnapsack(int[] wt, int[] val, int cap)

It must return the maximum total value achievable (the harness prints the returned double with exactly 2 decimals).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n item weights. Line 3: n item values. Line 4: the capacity cap.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum value, printed with 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= wt, val <= 1000, 1 <= cap <= 10000

questions.title: Cargo Van Loading
questions.description:
A delivery van has one capacity limit and the goal is to load as MANY orders as possible. The optimal greedy is to load the lightest orders first — an exchange argument shows no other choice fits more parcels. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int maxOrders(int[] weights, int cap)

It must return the maximum number of orders whose total weight fits in cap.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n order weights. Line 3: the van capacity cap.

Output Format:
One line with the number of orders loaded.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= weights <= 100, 1 <= cap <= 10000

questions.title: Carousel Cabin Count
questions.description:
A fairground carousel is modelled as a chain of cabins being assembled cabin by cabin; the operator needs the current count. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int dllLength(DNode head)

It must return the number of cabins (nodes) attached so far.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of cabins. Line 2: n space-separated integers — the cabin numbers in order.

Output Format:
One line with the cabin count.

1 <= n <= 10000, 1 <= cabin <= 100000

questions.title: Catalog Registration
questions.description:
A parts warehouse registers every new product code into a binary search tree so later lookups stay fast. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static TNode bstInsert(TNode root, int v)

It must insert the product code v into the search tree and return the root of the updated tree. The harness prints the inorder traversal, which lists the catalog in sorted order.

Line 1: n, the number of slots in the level-order description of the existing catalog tree. Line 2: n level-order integers, -1 marks a missing child. Line 3: the new code v.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted catalog after the insert, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= code, v <= 100000, all codes distinct, v is not already present

questions.title: Celebrity at the Party
questions.description:
At a party everyone is stacked in a lineup. A celebrity is known by everybody but knows nobody. Pairwise eliminations with a stack shrink the candidates to one.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int findCelebrity(int[][] know)

know[i][j] is 1 if person i knows person j, else 0. Return the index of the celebrity (known by all others and knowing nobody), or -1 if there is none.

Line 1: integer n.
Next n lines: n space-separated values of the matrix.

One line: the celebrity index or -1.

1 <= n <= 50

questions.title: Celsius to Fahrenheit
questions.description:
Convert a temperature with a floating-point method. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static double celsiusToFahrenheit(double c)

It must return F where F = C * 9 / 5 + 32. The harness prints the result rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with a real number C.

Output Format:
One line with the Fahrenheit value rounded to 2 decimals.

-100.0 <= C <= 100.0

questions.title: Cheapest Cable Offer

Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v w" — an offer to link poles u and v at price w.

questions.title: Cheapest Incident Edge
questions.description:

    static int cheapestEdge(int[][] m, int u)

Line 1: V. Then V lines, each with V space-separated weights — the symmetric adjacency matrix. Last line: the queried node u.

One line with the cheapest edge weight incident to u.

1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= weight <= 1000, 0 <= u < V

questions.title: Cinema Ticket Cost
questions.description:

    static int ticketCost(int adults, int children)

It must return adults * 150 + children * 80.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: the number of adults and the number of children.

Output Format:
One line with the total cost in rupees.

0 <= adults, children <= 50, adults + children >= 1

questions.title: Circular Queue Ring Buffer
questions.description:
A keyboard driver keeps keystrokes in a fixed-capacity ring buffer backed by a plain int array. You must implement it from scratch — no ArrayDeque or LinkedList allowed.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write exactly these three static methods:

    static void initQueue(int capacity)
    static int enqueue(int v)
    static int dequeue()

initQueue allocates the ring buffer for the given capacity (called once, first). enqueue stores v if there is room and returns 1, or returns 0 when the buffer is full. dequeue removes and returns the oldest value, or returns -1 when the buffer is empty. Use modular arithmetic on the array — the buffer must reuse freed slots.

Input Format:
Line 1: the capacity C.
Line 2: the number of operations m.
Next m lines: either "e x" (enqueue x) or "d" (dequeue).

Output Format:
One line per operation: enqueue prints 1 (success) or 0 (full); dequeue prints the value or -1 (empty).

Constraints:
1 <= C <= 1000
1 <= m <= 1000
-10000 <= x <= 10000

questions.description:
A warehouse app deletes every lowest-stock entry from its ArrayList and reports how many were cleared. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int removeMin(ArrayList<Integer> list)

questions.title: Climbing Stairs Count

You are climbing a staircase with n steps and can climb either 1 or 2 steps at a time. The number of distinct ways to reach the top follows the same recurrence as Fibonacci — the classic warm-up for counting DP, solved with two rolling variables. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long climbStairs(int n)

It must return the number of distinct orderings of 1-step and 2-step climbs that reach step n.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of ways.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Quicksort Recursion Depth
questions.description:
Lomuto quicksort with the last element as pivot builds a recursion tree; a bad pivot order drives it deep. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int quickDepth(int[] arr)

It must return the depth of the whole array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the recursion depth.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000000000 <= value <= 1000000000
